takeaway: Peak wind days are here. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) says the trade winds strengthen today while the air dries out, with clear skies on the North Pacific, Nicoya near 35°C, and gusts of 40–70 km/h on the Guanacaste lowlands (up to 85 km/h in the mountains). That is windier than yesterday's forecast. For surf, the Caribbean trades are firmly offshore at Nosara all week, strongest today through Thursday, so mornings are clean and afternoons can get blustery. No rainy spell and no tropical storm threat for the next two weeks.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Tue Nov 17 – Thu Nov 19)
periods.pattern: A dry air mass from the Caribbean and stronger high pressure there are pushing the trade winds hard across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica. IMN expects stable weather over most of the country, with only isolated afternoon storms on the South Pacific. The American and European ensemble averages and both main models show a fast northeast wind stream over Nicaragua and Guanacaste through Thursday. The European model has a small low over Nicaragua on Thursday, which is the usual heat low that forms on the downwind side when trades blow this hard, not a storm. The marine forecast mentions scattered showers offshore tonight, out over the water.
periods.implications: Sunny, hot (34–36°C afternoons), very breezy and dusty. Today through Thursday are the gustiest days; secure loose gear and be careful with any fire. Rain in Nosara is very unlikely.
periods.confidence: High on dry and windy. Moderate on how hard it gusts at the beach versus inland.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Fri Nov 20 – Mon Nov 23)
periods.pattern: The trades ease a notch but keep blowing. The marine forecast drops Papagayo to fresh east-northeast winds (15–20 knots) Friday and Saturday, then lighter (10–15 knots) Saturday night. The European ensemble average on Friday night still shows steady east-northeast flow over Central America, and the rain maps keep the wet stuff on the Caribbean coast. IMN's sub-seasonal outlook has the North Pacific at about 0–65 mm for the whole week of Nov 16–22, with a low chance of an extreme event.
periods.implications: Sunny, warm, a bit less wind, and more comfortable. A great stretch for outdoor plans and probably the easiest boat-trip days of the week by Sunday or Monday.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on day-to-day wind strength.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Tue Nov 24 – Tue Dec 1)
periods.pattern: The dry season holds. All three ensemble averages (American, European, and European AI) keep east to northeast trades across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through Dec 1, with a renewed push showing up near the end of November. Rain maps keep Nicoya very light; the European AI model shows some heavier rain around Nov 28 on Costa Rica's Caribbean side and Northern Zone, the classic trade-wind pattern, not on our coast. IMN expects the dry season to cover the whole Pacific side by Nov 23–29, with about 0–50 mm per week on the North Pacific and dry conditions into December.
periods.implications: Plan freely. Sunny, breezy days and hot afternoons. No rain gear needed in Nosara for most of this stretch.
periods.confidence: High on dry overall. Low on any single day's wind strength.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trade winds (northeast to east), meaning offshore at Nosara, all week. Strongest today through Thursday, easing Friday and the weekend. This clearly favors offshore over Pacific onshore.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued about 2:30 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 15–20 knots today, 20–25 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo tonight through Thursday (now 20–25 knots across the whole zone Thursday, stronger than yesterday's forecast), then 15–20 knots Friday and Saturday, and 10–15 knots Saturday night. South of the peninsula winds stay light and variable, so the trade wind comes over the land, not along the coast. Swell (open-ocean numbers, not beach heights): seas 6–8 ft at about 15–16 seconds through Thursday, but north of us much of that is wind-driven sea from the north and east; just south of the peninsula there's a cleaner southwest-to-west swell of 4–6 ft at up to 17 seconds Wednesday. Nicaragua should be offshore all day Tuesday through Thursday, which points to strong Nosara mornings, but Nosara is not necessarily offshore all day: the afternoon sea breeze can still turn it side-on, and when the trades do hold, the gusts can make faces ragged.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today through Thursday: dawn to late morning; offshore may hang on into the afternoon but it gets gusty and hard to paddle into. Friday to Monday: dawn through late morning, less wind and likely the most comfortable sessions of the week.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore all week. Moderate on how strong it gets at the beach and on afternoon sea-breeze timing.

gyreWatch.status: Not established. No watch needed. No prolonged rainy spell expected.
gyreWatch.supporting: Very little: scattered showers offshore tonight in the marine forecast, and small lows over Nicaragua on some model maps (heat lows from the strong trades, not storm systems).
gyreWatch.conflicting: Strong evidence against: strong northeast trades that push rain to the Caribbean side, all three ensemble averages light near Nicoya through about Nov 29, the hurricane center expecting no tropical storm formation in the next 7 days, IMN's sub-seasonal outlook calling the dry season set with a low chance of extreme events, and a global tropics outlook led by El Niño with lowered storm chances in the eastern Pacific.

whatChanged: Windier. IMN raised today's gusts on the Guanacaste lowlands to 40–70 km/h (yesterday's call was 20–50 km/h), and the marine forecast now keeps strong 20–25 knot trades through Thursday instead of easing Thursday. The easing shifts to Friday and the weekend. The rain outlook is unchanged: dry.
practical: Surf early every day; dawn to late morning is the window, and today through Thursday afternoons will be blustery. Drink plenty in 34–36°C heat. Tie down umbrellas and loose gear, watch for dust, and be extra careful with fire. Skip offshore boat or paddle trips through Friday. No rain plans needed.
alerts: No active IMN warnings for Guanacaste (last notice Nov 13 was about short heavy downpours in the Central Valley and Caribbean mountains).
IMN: wind gusts of 40–70 km/h on the North Pacific lowlands today, up to 85 km/h in the mountains.
Marine: strong northeast winds in the Gulf of Papagayo tonight through Thursday; rough water offshore.
